now.title: Agent Carter
now.text: In episode 1, Raymond sells Howard Stark's stolen formula to Leet Brannis, and a Leviathan assassin kills him.

proposed.text: In episode 1, Raymond buys Howard Stark's stolen Nitramene from Leet Brannis, and after Peggy takes it from his safe, a Leviathan assassin kills him.

changes.evidence: Raymond is the buyer, not the seller: he pays Brannis and puts the Nitramene bomb in his safe; Peggy steals it and Demidov shoots Raymond (Agent Carter S1E1).

now.title: Agent Carter
now.text: In episode 17, Thompson hands Masters over to Whitney Frost, who starts draining him with Zero Matter until she is interrupted.

proposed.text: In episode 19, Thompson hands Masters over to Whitney Frost, who starts draining him with Zero Matter until she is interrupted.

changes.evidence: Thompson's betrayal and Whitney absorbing Masters happen in AC209 (S2E9 'A Little Song and Dance' = series episode 19), not episode 17; fandom cites AC209 for the whole 'Betrayed by Thompson' section.

now.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
now.text: In episode 55, Werner joins Ward's HYDRA and attacks Andrew Garner. HYDRA leaves him in a coma, and S.H.I.E.L.D. takes him into custody.

proposed.text: In episode 55, S.H.I.E.L.D. wakes Werner from the coma Ward's HYDRA left him in after his failed attack on Andrew Garner, and questions him about Malick.

changes.evidence: The attack on Garner, the torture and the coma are in AoS306-307 (episodes 50-51); episode 55 ('Bouncing Back', AoS311) is where S.H.I.E.L.D. revives him from the coma and questions him about Malick. As written, the record's last event (coma, custody) is not in episode 55.

now.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
now.text: In episode 104, Fitz lets his Doctor side take over and forces surgery on Daisy to remove her inhibitor. Afterward, she locks him up.

proposed.text: In episode 104, Fitz lets his Doctor side take over and forces surgery on Daisy to remove her inhibitor. Afterward, she locks him up, until Simmons and Yo-Yo get Mack to free him.

changes.evidence: Fitz is released in 'Inside Voices' (episode 104): Simmons convinces Yo-Yo to help free Fitz and they get Mack to release him; in episode 105 he travels to England with Simmons and Yo-Yo. So 'In custody' is wrong for where episode 104 leaves him.

now.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
now.text: In episode 87, Radcliffe sends him out of the Framework. The real Fitz wakes up remembering every terrible thing he did.

changes.evidence: Radcliffe sends Fitz out of the Framework and he wakes at Ivanov's oil platform, where Aida runs the Framework; the platform is in the Baltic Sea, not Siberia (Siberia/Krasnoyarsk Krai is where the agents were kidnapped earlier). Use whatever place name the app has for Ivanov's platform.

now.title: Iron Fist S1
now.text: In episode 2, Ward has Danny locked in a psychiatric ward to keep him away from Rand Enterprises.

proposed.text: In episode 2, with Danny locked in a psychiatric hospital, Ward sends men posing as patients to kill him.

changes.evidence: Joy, not Ward, drugs Danny and has him institutionalized (end of episode 1). In episode 2 Ward ignores Harold and orders his men, disguised as patients, to kill Danny, who escapes.

proposed.title: Iron Fist S1
proposed.text: In episode 13, Ward sides with Danny and shoots Harold, who falls from the Rand Enterprises roof. Ward has the body cremated so he cannot come back.

changes.evidence: In the season 1 finale Ward allies with Danny, Colleen and Claire against Harold, shoots him off the Rand Enterprises rooftop and has the body cremated. The file goes straight from episode 9 to season 2 and never records his father's final death or his change of sides.

now.title: Iron Fist S2
now.text: In episode 4, Mary Walker is hired to watch Danny's allies, and her violent other self takes over.

proposed.text: In episode 4, Walker, a soldier hired by Joy and Davos to spy on Danny, drugs him and delivers him to the ritual that gives Davos the Iron Fist.

changes.evidence: In Iron Fist S2 the gentle 'Mary' is the alter and Walker is the mercenary; no violent self takes over in episode 4. In episode 4 Joy learns of Walker's dissociative identity disorder, and Walker attacks and drugs Rand and takes him to the ritual that moves the Iron Fist to Davos.

now.title: Captain Marvel
now.text: When Fury sees through his disguise, Talos tries to kill him, then tracks Vers to Maria Rambeau's home.

proposed.text: After Fury sees through his disguise, Talos follows Vers to Maria Rambeau's home. There he reveals that the Skrulls are refugees and wins her help.

changes.evidence: In the film Talos doesn't try to kill Fury after the Keller disguise is exposed. He arrives unarmed at Rambeau's home in Louisiana, says the Skrulls are refugees and plays the black box recording; he then fights beside Danvers, and she leaves to help the Skrulls find a home. 'At large' is wrong for where the film leaves him.

proposed.title: Loki S1
proposed.text: In episode 6, Sylvie sends Loki away and kills He Who Remains, setting loose the multiverse.
at: The Citadel at the End of Time

changes.evidence: In the season 1 finale ('For All Time. Always.') Sylvie sends Loki back to the TVA and kills He Who Remains, unleashing a multiverse the TVA cannot prune. This is her defining act and the file has no record of it.

now.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
now.text: Tarantula fights Spider-Man aboard a ship in New York Harbor.

proposed.text: Spider-Man stops Tarantula's smuggling operation on a passenger boat near the Williamsburg Bridge and captures him.

changes.evidence: Fandom: Tarantula ran a smuggling operation on a public passenger boat near the Williamsburg Bridge, and Spider-Man 'confronted and apprehended' him during the opening montage. Status should not be 'At large', and the boat is by the Williamsburg Bridge (the record's own at), not in New York Harbor.

now.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
now.text: In episode 55, corrupt Colombian police colonel Ramon executes Elena's cousin Francisco and holds Hunter and Morse captive.

proposed.text: In episode 55, corrupt Colombian police colonel Ramon executes Elena's cousin Francisco and holds Hunter and Morse captive, until Mack knocks him out and he is jailed.

changes.evidence: When S.H.I.E.L.D. storms the Bogota station in 'Bouncing Back' (AoS311), Mack knocks Ramon out; he is then imprisoned for corruption and later escapes before Slingshot (per fandom citing Slingshot ep 5). 'At large' is wrong for where episode 55 leaves him.

now.title: Luke Cage S1
now.text: In episode 11, Zip provides muscle for Cottonmouth. After Cottonmouth's death, Diamondback makes Zip one of his advisers.

proposed.text: In episode 9, Zip provides muscle for Cottonmouth. After Cottonmouth's death, Diamondback makes Zip one of his advisers.

changes.evidence: Zip goes to work for Shades and then Diamondback in LC108-LC109 (fandom 'Recruited by Diamondback' cites LC109). Episode 11 is the Harlem's Paradise hostage siege, which this record doesn't describe. So the last event is in episode 9.

owner_calls.question: Status after Iron Fist S1 episode 8: Danny beats Zhou Cheng until Claire and Colleen stop him; Claire checks his pulse and says he is 'not' okay, and he never appears again. Fandom gives his status as Unknown. Keep 'At large' or use 'Missing'?
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia says Rand 'almost beats Cheng to death'; fandom says status Unknown and gives no death.
